jobs.title: Program Manager of Community Nutrition and Food as Medicine Initiatives
jobs.description:
Guided by our mission of Feeding Neighbors, Nourishing Community, 4Saints Episcopal Food Pantry serves Fort Worth’s historic East Lancaster Avenue area by addressing the critical Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) that shape our community's well-being.

Located in a designated food desert, East Lancaster residents face systemic barriers to affordable, nutritious food—directly driving elevated rates of diet-related chronic illness and food insecurity.
4Saints acts as a bridge between healthcare systems and daily life. We address key Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) by pairing a dignified, client-choice food market with targeted clinical partnerships. By translating clinical care into accessible, nutritious food, practical education, and ongoing support, we empower neighbors to take control of their health in a welcoming, community-rooted environment.

Program Manager of Community Nutrition and Food as Medicine Initiatives

Position Type:
Full-Time / Grant-Funded (Initial 2-Year Term with renewal potential)

Position Summary:

The Program Manager of Community Nutrition and Food as Medicine Initiatives serves as 4Saints’ clinical and community nutrition leader, bridging community food access with measurable healthcare outcomes.

Reporting directly to the Executive Director, this role operates at two interconnected levels:
Shaping a high-nutrition food environment for all pantry guests.
Leading the continued growth of 4Saints' Food as Medicine initiative through the F.I.T. (Food as an Integrated Treatment) program.

As a Licensed Registered Dietitian, the Manager uses a dual approach to community health: driving broad-impact nutrition education, culinary classes, and pantry-wide strategic food sourcing, while providing high-touch 1:1 Medical Nutrition Therapy for F.I.T. program participants.

Working in close partnership with the Director of Operations (who manages physical facility operations, equipment, and inventory logistics), the Manager ensures that food procurement supports therapeutic health goals. As 4Saints expands its health initiatives, this position will also provide operational direction and supervision for growing program support staff, interdisciplinary team members, and academic interns.

This is a unique opportunity for an innovative Registered Dietitian to help shape an emerging Food as Medicine program. The Program Manager will have significant autonomy in designing systems, developing community partnerships, and building a sustainable model that integrates nutrition care with measurable health outcomes.

Key Responsibilities:

Community Health & Pantry- Wide Nutrition (Broad Impact)

Class & Workshop Facilitation:
Lead and conduct interactive group classes, workshops, and cooking demonstrations—focusing on nutrition education, chronic disease self-management (e.g., diabetes, hypertension), and practical culinary skills for pantry guests.
Choice-Based Market Experience:
Utilize 4Saints’ market floor to provide point-of-choice nutrition education, designing educational shelf-tagging, visual cues, and tours that help participants translate program concepts into independent grocery shopping habits.
Resource & Content Creation:
Author, design, and curate culturally responsive recipes, shopping guides, communication releases, class materials, and educational handouts in English and Spanish.

Food Ordering, Sourcing & Inventory Curation (In Partnership with Operations)

Food Procurement Leadership:
Provide nutritional leadership for pantry food procurement by guiding the selection and ordering of foods that support both community nutrition and therapeutic dietary goals. Work collaboratively with the Director of Operations on purchasing logistics, inventory capacity, and budget management.
Supplemental Sourcing & Vendor Vetting:
Research, vet, and establish alternative food sourcing channels (local growers, commercial distributors, food rescue networks) to supplement food bank offerings—ensuring consistent inventory/supply of high nutritional value foods for all clients.
Pantry Nutrition Curation:
Select and curate food items offered on the market floor, balancing core nutritious staples for broad pantry guests with specialized, medically tailored options (low-sodium, low-glycemic, DASH-compliant) required for F.I.T. participants.
Operational Alignment:
Work in close coordination with the Director of Operations to ensure placed orders align with established food budgets, storage/cold-chain capacity, and floor restocking workflows.

F.I.T. Program Leadership & Clinic Care (Targeted Impact)

F.I.T. Program Scaling:
Lead the continued expansion of the F.I.T. (Food as an Integrated Treatment) program, building upon its successful pilot phase to establish a sustainable Food as Medicine model that improves community health outcomes.
1:1 Clinical Coaching:
Conduct scheduled 1:1 consultations and follow-up Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) coaching sessions with F.I.T. participants—translating biometric data into tailored, goal-oriented health plans.
Closed-Loop Referral Pathways:
Design and refine workflows that translate incoming healthcare referrals and biometric data (e.g., blood pressure, A1C, cholesterol) into personalized market guidelines and client care plans.
Clinical Outcomes Tracking & Reporting:
Serve as primary liaison for data exchange with healthcare partners, tracking participant health metrics to evaluate and report clinical outcomes.

Organizational Leadership & Program Growth

Interdisciplinary Coordination:
Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary care strategies, integrating behavior-change models, health coaching methodologies, and client accountability practices as programming expands.
Team Supervision & Development:
Provide oversight, training, and direct supervision for designated program support personnel, health education staff, dietetic interns, academic rotations and volunteers.
Partnership Expansion:
Seek out and build strategic alliances with healthcare systems, community organizations, and specialized food suppliers to expand general pantry and Food as Medicine (F.I.T) program reach.
Organizational Alignment:
Collaborate effectively with Executive Leadership to align Food as Medicine initiatives with overarching organizational goals and evolving operational structures.
Culture & Equity:
Embed 4Saints’ commitment to dignity, respect, equity, and trauma-informed care across all participant touchpoints and operational workflows.

Qualifications & Requirements:

Required:

Credentials:
Active Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) credential and current State of Texas Dietitian License (or immediate eligibility for Texas licensure).
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Nutrition, Dietetics, Public Health, or a closely related field. Master's degree preferred.
Clinical Knowledge:
Practical experience delivering Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) for diabetes, metabolic conditions, and other therapeutic diets in a community-based setting.
Systems & Leadership Mindset:
Ability to build patient workflows, manage partner data exchanges, and lead interdisciplinary health teams or support staff.

Highly Preferred:

Language:
Bilingual fluency in Spanish and English (verbal and written) strongly preferred.
Experience:
2+ years in community nutrition, public health, ambulatory care, or clinical settings—with experience in client-choice pantry settings, hands-on cooking/shopping education, or vendor procurement.
Behavioral Health Expertise:
Experience applying behavior-change theories and health coaching methodologies preferred. Active credentials such as Certified Health & Wellness Coach (CHWC) or Certified Health Education Specialist (CHES) are considered a strong asset.
Supervisory Aptitude:
Demonstrated capacity to mentor, supervise, or lead direct reports, health coaches, students, or multidisciplinary team members.

Success in this role:

During the first year, the Program Manager will be expected to:
Expand participation in the F.I.T. Food as Medicine program.
Deliver engaging nutrition education and culinary programming for pantry guests.
Strengthen nutrition standards and strategic food procurement across the pantry.
Build and maintain referral partnerships with healthcare providers.
Track participant health outcomes and support grant reporting.
Help establish 4Saints as a regional leader in community-based Food as Medicine initiatives.

Compensation & Benefits:

Base Salary:
$55k–70k, commensurate with experience and qualifications
Performance Incentive Plan:
Opportunity to earn up to an additional 10% annual performance bonus, structured as:
5% linked to individual goal attainment (as defined by executive leadership).
5% contingent on the achievement of key organizational strategic objectives.

Annual Review:
Eligible for annual merit reviews (3–5% performance-based growth).
Technology Allowance:
$25 per month technology stipend.
Paid Time Off (PTO) & Leave:

3 weeks (15 days) of Paid Time Off (PTO).
10 days of paid sick/personal leave.
10 paid holidays (9 fixed holidays + 1 floating holiday).

Discretionary Holiday Leave:
One week off between Christmas and New Year's Day, subject to executive discretion and the operational requirements of 4Saints Episcopal Food Pantry.
Hybrid:
Work environment

jobs.description:
About Brandon J. Broderick, Attorney At Law

Brandon J. Broderick is a prestigious and forward-thinking law firm committed to delivering exceptional legal services. With a blend of tradition and innovation, we are dedicated to staying at the forefront of legal practice and technology. We care deeply about our clients and our employees and are committed to ensuring a supportive and inclusive environment where every team member can thrive and contribute to our collective success.

Overview

The primary responsibility of a legal intake specialist is to set up and manage the processes of onboarding new and prospective clients who are a good fit for our law firm. Some critical legal intake specialist job duties are:

Key Responsibilities

Interviewing prospective clients by phone and email to learn more about the Firm and familiarize them with their cases.
Conducting primary research to investigate whether prospective clients' claims have merit.
Evaluating prospective clients' claims to determine whether they're in line with the areas of practice and experience of the Firm.
Signing up new clients, gaining a client's business
Scheduling initial consultation appointments with attorneys for promising potential candidates
Enter client’s information for incoming and outgoing calls.

Key Traits

Bilingual: Spanish
Excellent telephone speaking voice, direct, clear, and concise.
Must be empathetic - Building trust through demonstrating a genuine understanding of the customer's situation.
Strong negotiation and people skills, demonstrating consistent and effective communication skills.
Sales experience is a strong plus!
Candidates must be driven, resilient, and persistent.
Must possess a solid hunger to succeed and grow.
Enjoy working in a team environment.
A natural salesperson, someone who can get clients to sign with us and who can handle all aspects of personal injury claims.
Enjoys phone interactions.
Someone fearless in going above and beyond for the client and the Firm will work flawlessly with our team of motivated and successful specialists and strong paralegal and administrative professionals.
Ability to solve problems and manage multiple tasks at once.
Positive and friendly demeanor.

If you are hungry to boost your career as an Intake Specialist, the opportunity is at our Firm. If you have the skill set to close clients on our services and present our Firm to clients in a way that demonstrates our ability to meet all their needs, you will be an excellent specialist for our Firm! Be inspired to increase your career knowledge and get motivated to become our Firm's next great intake specialist!

Highly Competitive Pay with Incentives

Compensation Range

$55,000—$60,000 USD

Compensation:
The base salary or hourly range for this position will be determined during the interview process and will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to; prior relevant experience, business needs and market factors. Additionally, salary wages are only part of the total compensation package.

Benefits: (Eligible full-time employees and part-time employees who work over 30 hours a week)

Medical Insurance including Dental and Vision
Paid Time off- Vacation and Sick time
Robust Holiday Schedule
Summer Fridays (Early closures Memorial Day- Labor Day)
401k Plans + matching for qualifying employees

Equal Opportunity Statement

Brandon J Broderick provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Position Title:
Team Leader Better Living (HM3) - Forensic Hospital, Malabar Justice Health - PFT

If you are passionate about delivering healthcare with the greatest impact, then come and join us at the Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network (JHFMHN). We are Just the Place
to grow your career and be part of a valued team delivering care where it's needed most!

Justice Health NSW is a challenging yet rewarding place to take your career even further. With industry-leading safety standards, you can focus on doing your best work alongside skilled colleagues while gaining job training to progress your career.

The Role

The Team Leader Better Living drives the provision of rehabilitation interventions and programs in the Forensic Hospital, coordinating contemporary, effective and recovery orientated mental health rehabilitation services for patients in The Forensic Hospital (TFH). The position will support and facilitate recovery initiatives and maximise opportunities for rehabilitation through operational oversight of multidisciplinary staff that provide support, recreational, and physical health care as per TFH governance structures. The position plays a lead role in duties designed to achieve individual recovery, focused on identified goals, in order to maximise opportunities for health and wellness; and achieving progress through evidence-based rehabilitation.

Essential Criteria

A degree and/or post graduate qualification in an allied health profession or a related field.
Demonstrated high level knowledge and understanding of best practice rehabilitation principles and current models of practice in forensic mental health for adults and adolescents.
Demonstrated experience in planning, implementing, and evaluating individual and group clinical rehabilitation interventions for persons with a mental illness in an inpatient setting.
Proven excellence in interpersonal and relationship management skills including the capacity to successfully relate to all levels of managers and staff as well as promoting community linkages and partnership building with clinical services, government, and non-government agencies.
Proven capacity to manage multi-disciplinary groups and build a strong collaborative culture.

Our Location, Team, and Service

The Forensic Hospital is a high-secure forensic mental health facility in New South Wales, operated by Justice Health NSW. This facility provides specialist, therapeutic inpatient care for adults and adolescent forensic, correctional, and high-risk civil patients.

A multidisciplinary team of medical, nursing, and allied health professionals are dedicated to providing a care across the clinical spectrum, from high dependency and acute care, to long stay and rehabilitation care.

While working at the Forensic Hospital you will develop strong professional connections with colleagues and making a positive contribution to vulnerable people. This dynamic work environment is interesting, stimulating, challenging, rewarding and one where you can have a positive impact on the lives of patients and their families.

To learn more about careers in our network, please click the links below:

Work for the Forensic Hospital — Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network (nsw.gov.au)

Why work with us — Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network (nsw.gov.au)

A mandatory and comprehensive two-week, full-time orientation is provided for all new staff at Forensic Hospital. All days are paid. The next intake dates will be 7-18 September 2026 and 12-23 October 2026.

Salary and Benefits

Your salary plus superannuation is just the beginning. You’ll have access to:

Access to salary packaging benefits.
A fitness passport (if you’re eligible) + ADOs (if full-time)
Free on-site parking to minimise your commute time.
Fantastic training & education opportunities available.

Diversity and Inclusivity

We are an equal-opportunity employer. We employ all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse groups, the LGBTQIA+ community, veterans, refugees, and people with disability.

We're working with JobAccess and the National Disability Recruitment Coordinator (NDRC) to remove barriers in our recruitment process and build a more inclusive workplace. If you require any adjustments to take part in this recruitment process, we're happy to discuss them with you.

This is also a Targeted Aboriginal Position. Preference will be given to applicants of Aboriginal descent. Exemption is claimed under Section 21 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977

Ready to Apply?

The first step is to submit your resume and answers to the following targeted questions:

Describe your experience leading a multidisciplinary team in a health setting. Include an example that demonstrates how you build a collaborative team culture.
Describe your experience supporting or improving the physical health care of patients in a mental health setting. Include an example of your role and the outcome.

Need more information?

Click here for the Position Description
Find out more about applying for this position

For role related queries or questions contact Jerome Chong on Jerome.Chong@health.nsw.gov.au

Applications Close: 25 August 2026 at 11:59pm AEST

Position Title:
Team Leader Better Living (HM3) - Forensic Hospital, Malabar Justice Health - PFT

If you are passionate about delivering healthcare with the greatest impact, then come and join us at the Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network (JHFMHN). We are Just the Place
to grow your career and be part of a valued team delivering care where it's needed most!

Justice Health NSW is a challenging yet rewarding place to take your career even further. With industry-leading safety standards, you can focus on doing your best work alongside skilled colleagues while gaining job training to progress your career.

The Role

The Team Leader Better Living drives the provision of rehabilitation interventions and programs in the Forensic Hospital, coordinating contemporary, effective and recovery orientated mental health rehabilitation services for patients in The Forensic Hospital (TFH). The position will support and facilitate recovery initiatives and maximise opportunities for rehabilitation through operational oversight of multidisciplinary staff that provide support, recreational, and physical health care as per TFH governance structures. The position plays a lead role in duties designed to achieve individual recovery, focused on identified goals, in order to maximise opportunities for health and wellness; and achieving progress through evidence-based rehabilitation.

Essential Criteria

A degree and/or post graduate qualification in an allied health profession or a related field.
Demonstrated high level knowledge and understanding of best practice rehabilitation principles and current models of practice in forensic mental health for adults and adolescents.
Demonstrated experience in planning, implementing, and evaluating individual and group clinical rehabilitation interventions for persons with a mental illness in an inpatient setting.
Proven excellence in interpersonal and relationship management skills including the capacity to successfully relate to all levels of managers and staff as well as promoting community linkages and partnership building with clinical services, government, and non-government agencies.
Proven capacity to manage multi-disciplinary groups and build a strong collaborative culture.

Our Location, Team, and Service

The Forensic Hospital is a high-secure forensic mental health facility in New South Wales, operated by Justice Health NSW. This facility provides specialist, therapeutic inpatient care for adults and adolescent forensic, correctional, and high-risk civil patients.

A multidisciplinary team of medical, nursing, and allied health professionals are dedicated to providing a care across the clinical spectrum, from high dependency and acute care, to long stay and rehabilitation care.

While working at the Forensic Hospital you will develop strong professional connections with colleagues and making a positive contribution to vulnerable people. This dynamic work environment is interesting, stimulating, challenging, rewarding and one where you can have a positive impact on the lives of patients and their families.

To learn more about careers in our network, please click the links below:

Work for the Forensic Hospital — Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network (nsw.gov.au)

Why work with us — Justice Health and Forensic Mental Health Network (nsw.gov.au)

A mandatory and comprehensive two-week, full-time orientation is provided for all new staff at Forensic Hospital. All days are paid. The next intake dates will be 7-18 September 2026 and 12-23 October 2026.

Salary and Benefits

Your salary plus superannuation is just the beginning. You’ll have access to:

Access to salary packaging benefits.
A fitness passport (if you’re eligible) + ADOs (if full-time)
Free on-site parking to minimise your commute time.
Fantastic training & education opportunities available.

Diversity and Inclusivity

We are an equal-opportunity employer. We employ all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse groups, the LGBTQIA+ community, veterans, refugees, and people with disability.

We're working with JobAccess and the National Disability Recruitment Coordinator (NDRC) to remove barriers in our recruitment process and build a more inclusive workplace. If you require any adjustments to take part in this recruitment process, we're happy to discuss them with you.

This is also a Targeted Aboriginal Position. Preference will be given to applicants of Aboriginal descent. Exemption is claimed under Section 21 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977
